b.answer:
Worked example: Ibadan Tiles Centre, a fictional tiles shop selling to builders and households.

ChannelWho answersReply rulesReply time now
WhatsApp (shop phone)Shop managerFree-form within 24 h; templates afterAbout 3 h
EmailOwnerFull sentences; quotes and invoices1 to 2 days
Instagram DMs and commentsOwner's nephew24-hour DM window; no details in publicEvenings only
Facebook commentsNobody regularlyPublic: one line; move personal things to DMOften never
Phone callsWhoever is freeCall-backs noted on paperSame day, sometimes

Matching rules: merge on a verified phone (stored as +234…) or lowercase email from an invoice; link but verify when someone types a number in another channel; suggest to the owner when a business name is similar; never merge on a personal name alone.

Response targets: questions 5 minutes (agent), order problems 15 minutes, complaints a person within 1 working hour; each conversation assigned to a named person.

Two-channel example found: a contractor emailed for a quote on Monday, then asked on WhatsApp on Tuesday "did you see my email?" and got a second, different price from the manager.

Owner signed the map on 2 October.
mistakes: Listing channels without who answers them or how long replies take now.
Matching rules that allow a merge on a name.
Targets owned by 'the team' instead of a named person.
Skipping the hunt for a real two-channel customer.
b.pass: A map of every channel with owner, rules and current reply time, matching rules (merge, verify, suggest, separate), response targets, one real case of a customer on two channels, and the owner's agreement.
b.redo: Send it back if names can trigger a merge, any channel has no owner, or the owner has not agreed the map.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane, email and WhatsApp into one Supabase record and one agent.

  1. Adapters: Gmail Trigger and the 5.1 WhatsApp webhook, each producing { channel, thread_id, from_value, from_type, text, received_at, raw_id } and calling Inbox · Receive.
  2. Normalise (lesson's Code node): phones to +234…, emails trimmed and lowercase.
  3. Supabase: find a verified identity with that value → that customer; none → new customer, unverified identity. A phone or email typed in the text that matches another customer → link suggestion and needs_verification = true, never a merge.
  4. Upsert the open conversation for that order; update last_customer_msg_at and reply_channel.
  5. Agent with get_customer_context (timeline, open orders, decisions). System message: reply only on reply_channel, in its style; no order or payment details if needs_verification.
  6. Switch on reply_channel → Gmail or WhatsApp sender; other open threads get "We've replied on WhatsApp so everything's in one place" and close.

Test 1: you email from funke.a@example.com about HL-0412, then WhatsApp from +2348030001111 (both verified at checkout).

TableRows after test
customers1 (Funke Adeyemi)
identitiesemail, phone: both verified
conversations1, reply_channel = whatsapp
messages2 in, 1 out (WhatsApp), 1 note (email)

Test 2: a friend writes from funke.a.other@example.com as "Funke A." asking about a different order. Result: a second customer, nothing shared, no link suggested.

Evidence: Supabase screenshots after each test and both execution logs.
mistakes: Not normalising phones, so 0803…, 234803… and +234803… become three customers.
Merging when a customer types someone's number instead of linking and verifying.
Replying on both channels instead of once on the latest.
The agent not reading the decisions table before replying.
s.pass: Supabase screenshots show one customer, one conversation and one reply on WhatsApp for the two-channel test, and two separate customers with nothing shared for the namesake test.
s.redo: Send it back if the same person became two customers, the namesakes were merged or linked, or the customer got two replies.

g.answer:
Worked example: Ibadan Tiles Centre (fictional) running one inbox across WhatsApp, email and Instagram for two weeks.

ChannelMedian first reply beforeAfterMissed targets
WhatsApp3 h 10 min2 min1 (complaint, Saturday)
Email26 h11 min0
Instagram9 h3 min2 (order problems, evenings)

Merges: 64 automatic (verified phone or email); 9 suggested: 6 confirmed after a code was sent or the customer answered, 3 rejected (same first name, different people). Wrong merges: 0, checked by the owner reviewing every merge on Fridays.

Consistency: two customers asked about the same refund on two channels; both got one answer on their latest channel, matching the decisions table.

Normalisation clean-up: before go-live, 412 old contacts in mixed phone formats became 247 customers.

What changed for the team: the manager owns WhatsApp and order problems, the owner owns complaints and quotes over ₦500,000; the 18:00 digest replaced the evening phone round-up.

Next step: add Facebook comments in week 3, and move evening Instagram order problems to the manager's phone.

Submit: the before and after table with how "before" was measured (WhatsApp and email timestamps from the previous two weeks), the merge log with decisions, the missed-target alerts and the owner's note.
mistakes: No measured baseline for response times.
Counting automatic merges without anyone checking them.
Reporting one overall response time instead of one per channel.
Leaving missed targets out of the report.
g.pass: Two weeks on three or more channels with median response time per channel against the previous two weeks, merges made and suggested, missed targets, and zero wrong merges confirmed by a review.
g.redo: Send it back if any wrong merge happened, response times did not improve, or the merge counts are missing.
